judgment.rationale: Both indicators sit in BASIC 1, Strand 4: Writing (same coordinate rank 0), so direction rests on statement content rather than rank. The second SFI (B1.4.2.1.1, 'Copy letters of the alphabet clearly', Sub-Strand 2: Penmanship, under Content Standard B1.4.2.1 'Copy and write letters of the alphabet correctly') is letter-level handwriting control: forming individual alphabet letters legibly by copying. The first SFI (B1.4.3.1.3, 'Write words using both capital and small letters', Sub-Strand 3: Writing Letters – Small and Capital, under B1.4.3.1 'Use general skills strategies and knowledge of letter sounds to write legibly and boldly') extends that control from copied single letters to independently written whole words combining capital and small forms. Proficiency in clear letter copying substantively supports success at writing words in mixed case, so the source is the second SFI. The shared token 'letters' alone would be insufficient, but the letter-to-word and copy-to-independent-write expansion across the two Writing sub-strands is pair-specific and instructionally coherent. Source excerpts for both endpoints are truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and both endpoints and their ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, which limits but does not contradict this reading.
